territorial_scope.description: Amends a federal statute (Defense Production Act of 1950) and applies to federal agencies and facilities in the United States.

evidence.quote: Title III of the Defense Production Act of 1950 (50 U.S.C. 4531 et seq.) is amended

summary.short: Adds Sec. 306 to the Defense Production Act of 1950 on critical AI infrastructure (data centers of 50 MW or more, dispatchable power plants, transmission, fuel supply). Lets the President designate covered projects as priority national defense projects, coordinate federal permits, and authorize financial assistance for baseload power facilities.
summary.long: The bill, introduced and pending, amends Title III of the Defense Production Act of 1950 by adding Sec. 306. Critical AI infrastructure includes data centers or high-performance computing facilities with at least 50 MW of connected load dedicated primarily to AI, dispatchable baseload generation of at least 100 MW, associated high-voltage transmission, and essential fuel supply infrastructure. The President may designate covered projects as priority national defense projects. For designated projects the President must require federal agencies to review permits concurrently under a consolidated schedule, with federal authorizations to be completed within 2 years of a complete application unless extraordinary circumstances require more time. Agency failure to follow the schedule is treated as a failure to act under 5 U.S.C. 706(1). The President resolves inter-agency disputes, and a single lead agency prepares environmental reviews. Civil actions have a 60-day filing window, with Circuit-court venue and limits on injunctions and vacatur. The President may exempt designated projects from new emissions limitations by executive order if defense necessity is determined and published. The United States must compensate owners or operators for federal changes that prohibit or materially impair a designated facility for at least 180 days, subject to claim deadlines and exclusions. Eligible facilities may receive Title III financial assistance covering up to 90 percent of project costs, and guidance is due within 180 days of enactment. A conforming amendment adds the designated infrastructure to Sec. 702(14). The text states no enactment date for the new provisions.

No legal_basis or enacted_by_bill relation is stated in the text. target_instrument_id is left empty because no registry match was checked. Internal issues: (1) Sec. 306(h)(1) refers to a coal-fueled facility meeting subsection (a)(2)(A)-(C) and contractually dedicated under subsection (a)(2)(D), but (a)(2)(D) defines fuel supply infrastructure and the contract condition appears in (a)(2)(B)(iv). (2) Sec. 306(f) and Sec. 306(g)(4) refer to section 702 and section 304 of this Act, which are sections of the Defense Production Act, not of this bill. Sec. 306(j) refers to Rural Utilities Service financing, which is not coded as an instrument.
